criteria.criterion: A git test in crates/athena-git shows that show_file on a directory path (for example a tree such as 'docs/' or 'docs') returns Ok(None) with no error, and that it still returns the bytes for a real file. Run: cargo test -p athena-git.
criteria.evidence: The test show_file_on_a_directory_is_none_not_an_error passed. It asserts show_file(head, "docs") and show_file(head, "docs/") are Ok(None), and that show_file(head, "docs/a.md") is Some(b"a"). show_file now asks git for the object type (cat-file -t) and returns None for anything that is not a blob.

criteria.criterion: A test with a fake planner whose plan lists 'docs/' shows that Athena emits a major finding for that path, that the job moves on to the next plan round, and that nothing crashes or returns an error. Run: cargo test.
criteria.evidence: a_plan_that_lists_a_directory_gets_a_major_athena_finding_and_the_job_goes_to_the_next_round passed, along with the other 22 job_plan tests. It covers docs/ (create), src (create) and src (modify). For each one it checks: go() returns Ok, the job lands, the planner runs twice and the critic once, round 1's critique is Revise with no critic call, and it holds an Athena major finding that names the path.

criteria.criterion: Plan checks give a major finding, not an error, for any planned path that is a directory, is absolute, contains '..', is empty, or ends in '/'. A unit test covers each case. Run: cargo test.
criteria.evidence: The unit test passed. It covers docs/, docs, src/deep (directories), the empty string, whitespace, /etc/passwd, C:/x.txt, ../x.rs, a/../b.rs, a\..\b.rs and src/: each gets exactly one Athena major finding. Plain paths (src/new.rs, a..b.rs, docs/new.md) get no major finding. path_problem returns an Option and the caller adds a finding; there is no error path. JobPlan::validate does not check paths, so these paths reach plan_findings in the real flow.

criteria.criterion: cargo test --locked, cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings and cargo fmt --check all pass, as does xtask's boundary test.
criteria.evidence: Athena reported that fmt --check, clippy --all-targets --locked -D warnings and cargo test --locked (933 tests) all passed on this tree. I ran the xtask tests myself: tests/policy.rs passed, including the_boundary_scanner_flags_a_planted_term and athena_refers_to_no_one_who_runs_it_or_where (9/9).

criteria.criterion: athena.toml has [job_plan] enabled = true, and no other setting in that file changes.
criteria.evidence: The diff for athena.toml changes one line, enabled = false to enabled = true, under [job_plan].

criteria.criterion: CHANGELOG.md under [Unreleased] names the job-planning crash on a directory path and job 20261017-204355-358k.
criteria.evidence: Under [Unreleased], a new ### Fixed entry names job 20261017-204355-358k, the docs/ path, the 'git cat-file blob <base>:docs/ failed' error, its root cause, the fix and the re-enabled setting.

criteria.criterion: Outcome check: replaying the failing input, a plan that lists docs/, no longer produces the 'git cat-file blob <base>:docs/ failed' error. This is shown by the new tests failing on the old code and passing on the new.
criteria.evidence: The new tests pass on the candidate. I did not run them on the old code, because I may not change the tree. From reading the code: the old show_file ran cat-file -e, which succeeds for a tree, then cat-file blob, which fails on a tree. So the git test's show_file(head, "docs").unwrap() would panic, and the test would not even compile, since it calls path_is_tree. The integration test's plan lists "src", which plan_record's exists closure in run.rs:553 passes to show_file. On the old code that returns an error that propagates out of go(), so the test's .unwrap() would fail. That is the reported crash.

findings.summary: The drive-letter check treats any path whose second byte is ':' (for example 'a:b.rs') as absolute.
findings.evidence: path.as_bytes().get(1) == Some(&b':') flags any one-character prefix followed by a colon, not only a drive letter such as C:. This is harmless in practice, but a little broader than its message says.

findings.summary: show_file now runs three git processes for a file instead of two (cat-file -e, -t, then blob).
findings.evidence: object_type runs cat-file -e and then cat-file -t. Running cat-file -t alone with its exit code checked would be enough. This is a small cost, not a correctness problem.

summary: The change fixes the root cause. Git::show_file now checks the object type and returns None for anything that is not a blob, so no caller can crash on a directory. The plan checks in admission.rs now give a major Athena finding, which sends the plan back without calling the critic, for a planned path that is empty, absolute, contains '..', ends in '/', or is a directory in the base commit. athena.toml re-enables [job_plan] and changes nothing else, and CHANGELOG.md names the crash and job 20261017-204355-358k. I ran the new git test, the plan-path unit test, all 23 job_plan integration tests and xtask's policy and boundary tests, and all passed. Athena reported that fmt, clippy and the full test suite also passed. I did not run the new tests on the old code. Reading it shows they would fail there: the old show_file errors on a tree, and that is the reported crash. Every changed file is on the deliverables list. Two nits only, so the verdict is pass.
